title: Modality class — one line of the cancer-treatment census, and what it does or does not reach in EMC
_role: Every MOD-* validates against this. A modality class is a CATEGORY OF TREATMENT that exists in oncology somewhere, independent of whether this program has ever looked at it. That independence is the point: routes.json records what we chose to pursue, and this records the space that choice was made from, so `nobody has looked at this` becomes a query rather than a recollection.
_not_a_target_register: ⛔ THE AXIS IS MODALITY, NEVER TARGET. `CD276-directed ADC` is not a row; `antibody-drug conjugate` is, and the CD276 question lives in `requires` and in the surface-antigen artifacts that own it. The two axes were deliberately separated because a target census keyed by modality would duplicate every antigen once per delivery format, and the resulting matrix would be maintained in neither place.

name.description: The class as the field names it, not as this repository nicknames it. A reader who searches the literature for this string should land on the class.

band.description: The four bands exist because three of them were STRUCTURALLY INVISIBLE to every prior search here (emc-unexplored-treatment-lanes.md §0). A census that carried only `drug_mechanism` would reproduce the blind spot it was built to measure.

group.description: The nineteen groups partition the census. A group is a place to look, not a claim -- two rows in one group may end in opposite verdicts.

parent.description: The broader class this refines, when the row is a sub-form whose EMC verdict differs from its parent's. Used SPARINGLY: a sub-form that shares its parent's verdict and reasons is not a row, it is an example inside one.

exemplar.description: A named agent or platform that instantiates the class, so a reader can tell which class is meant. ⚠ NAMING ONE IS NOT A CLINICAL CLAIM about it, and must never be written as one -- the string identifies the category and says nothing about what the agent does in EMC.

verdict.description: `in_clinical_use` is the BASELINE and exists because a census with no denominator for the incumbents cannot say what an unexplored option would have to beat -- trimcrae's question was framed as `a pretty small arsenal`, and the size of that arsenal is a measurement this register should carry rather than imply. It is NOT a claim about how well anything works. `already_rejected` and `excluded` are deliberately separate. The first means SOMEONE ELSE HERE ALREADY SETTLED IT and the row's job is to POINT at that ruling and never to restate its reason (rule 1); the second means this census is the thing doing the closing, and then the reason belongs here because here is its only home. Collapsing them would either duplicate ~50 existing rulings or hide which document owns each.

prior_coverage.description: ⭐ THIS FIELD IS THE CENSUS'S RESULT; everything else is bookkeeping. `searched_before` means a prior sweep here demonstrably pointed at this class. `never_searched` means no prior document did -- which is not the same as `rejected`, and the whole reason a census differs from a search is that only a census can tell them apart.

prior_ref.description: The document that already considered this class. REQUIRED whenever `prior_coverage` is `searched_before` or `verdict` is `already_rejected`. Checked by [P1]/[P2] like every other pointer, so a rejection cannot be attributed to a document that does not say it.

route.description: The route that covers this class. REQUIRED when `verdict` is `on_board` -- an on_board claim with no route is exactly the unverifiable coverage assertion this collection exists to prevent.

rationale.description: Why this verdict, for THIS disease. For `already_rejected` this states only WHAT was ruled and by whom; the argument stays in the owning document.

requires.description: What EMC would have to possess for the class to reach it -- an address, a biomarker, a dependency, an accessible compartment. This is where the target axis is allowed to touch the modality axis, and only as a stated precondition.

blockers.description: Registered blockers this class runs into. A row may name a blocker without any route naming it -- the class can be blocked before anyone has proposed a route through it.

revisit_trigger.description: REQUIRED when `verdict` is `parked_capability`. Same discipline as a route's: a park with no named way back is indistinguishable from a closure nobody wanted to write.

zero_dollar_next_step.description: The cheapest observation that would move this row. CLAUDE.md §0: most rows that read blocked are waiting on a free CI fetch, a regeneration or a lookup, and naming that step is what stops `blocked` being asserted rather than checked.

provenance.description: Where this row's verdict is owned. Defaults to this collection.
